Hi all,

Short technical runbook and preliminary expected outcomes so everyone's aligned:

Runbook summary:
- 07/02 06:00–10:00 PT primary window (we'll perform a dry-run 07/01 22:00–22:30 PT if ops can spare a quick smoke test).
- Tests:
  * Steady-state 60m at 80 concurrent sessions (mix: 60% chat short prompts, 40% medium-long generation).
  * Spike sequence: step up 20 -> 40 -> 80 -> 120 concurrent over 10 minutes, hold 5 minutes each.
  * Concurrency ramp: slow ramp from 10 -> 120 over 30 minutes to observe queuing and KV cache behavior.
- Metrics collected: TTFT, p50/p95/p99 latency per token and per response, tokens/sec, 429/5xx rates, and per-instance GPU utilization (if shared).
- Acceptance: p95 TTFT <= 350ms on short prompts, sustained tokens/sec within 10% of Redwood predicted baseline for the chosen model config, and <1% error rate.

Preliminary run notes (from internal dry-run against a comparable config):
- Steady-state (80 concurrent) p95 TTFT: 310ms; tokens/sec ~ 18k; error 0.2%
- Spike to 120 concurrency produced brief p95 bumps to ~520ms for ~60s but TTL recovered when KV cache warmed; overall error remained <1%

I'll attach the dry-run PDF with charts. During the run we suggest a Slack channel #acme-load-test for real-time alerts and one dedicated Redwood engineer on-call to triage.

Rishi
